$comment: Every change to the base witness (corrections) and every letter difference of the other witnesses (variants), classified. Proven by check.py.

corrections.reason: The base file reads निचाय्य मां (‘having perceived me’) where GRETIL, the vishvAsa mūla and Madhva’s text all read निचाय्येमां (nicāyya imāṃ, ‘having perceived this [peace]’); Śaṅkara’s gloss in the same file comments on imām: «निचाय्य दृष्ट्वा चात्मभावेन इमां स्वबुद्धिप्रत्यक्षां शान्तिम्».

The base file reads अग्न्यया; GRETIL, the vishvAsa mūla and Madhva’s text read अग्र्यया (agryayā, ‘sharp, foremost’), and Śaṅkara derives the word from agra, ‘point’ («अग्रमिव»), which gives agryā — the base file’s bhāṣya repeats the same slip of न्य for र्य in its quotation.
The base file reads निर्हितो, an extra र्; GRETIL, the vishvAsa mūla and Madhva’s text read निहितो (nihitaḥ, ‘placed’), and Śaṅkara’s gloss in the same file reads «उत्तराधरारण्योर्निहितः».

variants.note: GRETIL writes the final m of tṛtīyam before the danda it inserts (तृतीयम् ।); the same word.
GRETIL reads अवत्सीर्, short a; the s-aorist of vas ‘dwell’ is avātsīḥ, as AS, the vishvAsa mūla and Madhva’s text read and Śaṅkara glosses.
GRETIL reads punar āha, ‘spoke again’, without eva; AS and the vishvAsa mūla read punar evāha, which Śaṅkara comments on. Madhva’s text agrees with GRETIL.

GRETIL reads sujñeyam, ‘easy to know’, where AS and the vishvAsa mūla read suvijñeyam, ‘easy to know well’ (Śaṅkara: सुष्ठु विज्ञेयम्). The shorter form keeps the triṣṭubh pāda at eleven syllables; Madhva’s text reads sujñeyaḥ.
